title: Triangles and Quadrilaterals by Angles Practice
description: Practice checking triangle and quadrilateral angle conditions.

questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of any triangle?
questions.explanation: The three interior angles of every triangle add to 180 degrees.

questions.question: Can a triangle have angles 40 degrees, 60 degrees, and 80 degrees?
options: Yes, because the angles add to 180 degrees
Yes, because all angles are acute
No, because the angles add to 160 degrees
No, because a triangle must have a right angle

questions.question: A triangle has angles 55 degrees, 75 degrees, and x. What is x? Enter just the number.
A triangle with angles 90 degrees, 60 degrees, and 40 degrees is possible.
What is the sum of the interior angles of any quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: The four interior angles of every quadrilateral add to 360 degrees.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has angles 80 degrees, 100 degrees, 90 degrees, and x. What is x? Enter just the number.
Which set of angles can form a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: 90 + 90 + 90 + 90 = 360, so this set can form a quadrilateral.

questions.question: Explain whether a triangle with angles 30 degrees, 70 degrees, and 90 degrees is possible.
questions.correctAnswer: It is impossible because 30 + 70 + 90 = 190, but triangle angles must add to 180 degrees.
questions.explanation: A correct explanation must compare the angle sum to 180 degrees.
